projects.title: Echo(logies): Data Through Design 2026 at BRIC
projects.description: Annual data art exhibition at BRIC House Gallery in Brooklyn, featuring ten projects that creatively interpret NYC Open Data, on display through April 5.
projects.why_interesting: Includes projects like Turnstile Murmurations, Urban Data Orchestra, and The Oracle of Gotham -- all built from NYC open datasets and turned into physical/interactive art.

projects.title: Visualizing the Internet (2026 edition)
projects.description: Interactive map of undersea fiber-optic cables, peering bandwidth by city, and IP address distribution via BGP, animated year by year.
projects.why_interesting: Elegant infrastructure mapping with new dynamic city clustering, SVG export, and open JSON datasets from TeleGeography and PeeringDB.

projects.title: I3: Infrastructure Intelligence Index preview
projects.description: New open data layer for developers and planners previewed at NYC School of Data 2026, purpose-built for city infrastructure analysis.
projects.why_interesting: BetaNYC previewed this at the March 28-29 event -- a new structured data layer specifically designed for infrastructure planning and civic tech.

projects.title: Washington Post: spring arrival timing across the U.S.
projects.description: Interactive visualization tracking the exceptionally early 2026 spring across the U.S., using National Phenology Network data with cherry blossom bloom timelines.
projects.why_interesting: Published April 10 -- city-level selector lets you compare your location's bloom timing against historical averages, with daily temperature overlays.

projects.title: NYU Re/presenting Data: urban data visualization contest
projects.description: NYU Data Services ran an urban data visualization contest with 30+ submissions, exhibited at 370 Jay Street on April 9.
projects.why_interesting: A fresh crop of student and researcher urban data visualizations, all built with NYC-area data, just went on display this week.

projects.title: OSCUR: open-source cyberinfrastructure for urban computing
projects.description: Multi-institutional platform funded by a $5M NSF grant to build an open-source ecosystem of tools for transforming city data into actionable knowledge.
projects.why_interesting: Major federal investment in open tooling for urban data analysis, led by UIC with partners across institutions.

projects.title: CityPulse: urban mobility risk intelligence platform
projects.description: Platform combining H3 geospatial indexing, ML demand/risk scoring, LLM natural language analytics, and an MCP server for urban mobility data.
projects.why_interesting: Interesting blend of cutting-edge tech (H3, LLMs, MCP protocol) applied specifically to urban mobility risk assessment.
